sections.content: How many people are "early education and childcare assistants"?

117,255 people

were counted on the census as "early education and childcare assistants" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Early education and childcare assistants assist in the care of children from birth up to seven years of age in day or residential nurseries, children�s homes, maternity units and similar establishments.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "early education and childcare assistants" there were more women than men (97.3% compared with 2.7%).

This means "early education and childcare assistants" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "caring personal service occupations".

Men made up 2.7% and women made up 97.3% of "early education and childcare assistants"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "early education and childcare assistants" included:

  • dental nurses
  • early education and childcare practitioners
  • registered children's nurses

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 20 to 24 years. Of the whole working population 7.9% were aged 20 to 24 years. For people working as "early education and childcare assistants", 17.3% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "early education and childcare assistants" was 65 years or older.

We can look at who worked as "early education and childcare assistants" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

There is a higher number of women than men with this occupation across all age groups. The age profile for men and women is shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "early education and childcare assistants" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "early education and childcare assistants", 9.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (51.6% compared with 48.4%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (98.5%) than self-employed (1.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
